subject: Dedicated pool oversubscription — capacity delta and procurement path
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: ops@edgebank.com, procurement@edgebank.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated pool oversubscription — capacity delta and procurement path

Hi all,

Quick flag from our monitoring: the dedicated GPU pool serving EdgeBank has been oversubscribed for the last 18 hours. We've observed a steady uptick in 5xxs (predominantly 502s) and a 3–5x increase in median token latency during peak windows. Attached is a short export of metrics (edgebank-metrics-20260219.csv) and a one-page capacity request (capacity-request-edgebank.pdf).

Key points:
- Current reserved throughput contract is being exceeded by variable peaks — sustained for multiple windows.
- Error rate and tail latency are now impacting customer-facing retries; ops team has flagged failed transactions.
- We need an operational mitigation (short-term) and a procurement path (medium-term) to avoid repeated customer-visible errors.

As next steps I recommend:
1) Approve an emergency temporary capacity allocation (24–72h) while we stabilize.
2) David to validate low-friction config changes (model variant fallback / quantized serving) that can be rolled in <3 hours.
3) Procurement to prioritize an addendum for reserved capacity and credits for incident exposure.

EdgeBank team — can you confirm impact on your side (retries, backoffs) and whether procurement can accept an expedited amendment?

I’ll hold a short ops call at 09:00 PT to walk through mitigation options unless you ask otherwise.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: edgebank-metrics-20260219.csv, capacity-request-edgebank.pdf

On Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 08:34 AM EdgeBank Operations <ops@edgebank.com> wrote:
> Marissa —
>
> Thanks for the alert and the files. We're seeing increased error volume on our side ...

Quick technical readout:
- Root cause (short): sudden shift in request profile — average sequence length rose ~2.3x after a traffic change from a partner integration; this increases per-request GPU working set and KV pressure.
- Observed consequences: KV cache churn -> more cross-shard traffic -> higher token latency -> queueing -> 502s.

Practical mitigation options (ordered by speed to deploy):
A) Serve quantized model variant for EdgeBank traffic only (low latency regression, ~1–2 hrs to validate + deploy to route). Minimal infra change.
B) Provision temporary dedicated nodes (3 x p4-style equivalents) for 48–72 hours. Fastest to remove pressure but needs procurement sign-off and cost approval.
C) Apply per-customer rate shaping + soft queue to smooth peaks (low immediate cost, moderate dev time — ~6–8 hrs to tune).

I uploaded a short capacity request (capacity-request-edgebank.pdf) with estimated costs and a short Drive folder (https://drive.redwood.com/edgebank/capacity-analysis-2026-02-19).

Recommendation: pursue A immediately while we stand up B in parallel if procurement can sign an emergency addendum. If procurement needs internal approval, we should document the delta and cost — I can own the ops side of that doc.

— David
David Kim
Infrastructure Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity-request-edgebank.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: ops@edgebank.com, procurement@edgebank.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool oversubscription — capacity delta and procurement path

Team —

Summarizing for executive decisioning and procurement path:
- Immediate pain: EdgeBank is seeing user-facing failures tied to our dedicated pool oversubscription. Ops reports checkout failures during peak windows.
- Short-term action (cost and impact): implement David's Option A (quantized model variant) now — estimated 1–3 hours to route and validate; expected to materially reduce tail latency with negligible functional degradation.
- Contingency (costy): provision temporary capacity (Option B) for 48–72 hrs. Estimated one-time delta is in the attached PDF; procurement link above.

Ask: Vivek / Mina — please approve the emergency capacity addendum (EDGE-2025-0497 amendment) if procurement confirms they cannot expedite within the next 2 hours. I will coordinate the ops call and confirm when Option A is live.

If we don't get a sign-off, we will need to implement conservative rate shaping immediately which will reduce throughput for some user journeys and may cause business disruption.

Thanks — I will escalate to the exec on-call if we do not have an answer by 17:30 PT.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
